task.description:
REQ-ANALYST drafted REQ-003 (owner FRONTEND-DEV, depends_on [REQ-001a, REQ-001b]: add 'en' to src/i18n/routing.ts's locales array, keep defaultLocale 'ru', seed messages/en.json with Russian-duplicated placeholders matching messages/ru.json's 177-key set) and REQ-004 (owner CONTENT-BA, depends_on [REQ-003]: write real English copy for all 177 messages/en.json keys, explicitly deciding the domain-vocabulary-in-English question) into docs/agents/requirements.yaml, in response to GitHub issue #3 ('translate to en'). Run WF-01 Step 2's full gate against both: TESTABILITY, CONSISTENCY, DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS, DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT, SIZE. Read both entries directly from docs/agents/requirements.yaml (grep for 'id: REQ-003' / 'id: REQ-004' — they start at lines 180 and 251) rather than trusting this summary.

Pay particular attention to: (a) REQ-ANALYST's own handoff (handoffs/WF01-ISSUE3-EN-LOCALE/step-01-req-analyst.json, result.issues) flagged a MINOR finding that the switcher mechanism is simpler than originally assumed — src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx now iterates routing.locales generically, so adding 'en' to the array alone should produce a working three-way switcher with no separate switcher-code change needed. Verify this claim yourself by reading LocaleSwitcher.tsx directly, and check whether REQ-003's description/acceptance criteria correctly reflect this (not stale REQ-001a-era framing about hardcoded switcher JSX). (b) Whether REQ-003's decision to keep defaultLocale='ru' is stated with reasoning, not just asserted. (c) Whether REQ-004's acceptance criteria are mechanically checkable (script/diff against messages/ru.json's key set) as claimed. (d) Whether REQ-004's domain-vocabulary-in-English decision is a legitimate unilateral call or should have been escalated — note this is a genuinely different question from the ru/uz precedent (there, domain terms stayed English inside non-English copy; here the whole locale IS English, so 'keep verbatim' has a different meaning) — assess with real scrutiny, don't just accept REQ-ANALYST's framing. (e) depends_on correctness: REQ-003 lists [REQ-001a, REQ-001b] — confirm those are actually the right prerequisites (i.e. REQ-003 genuinely needs the locale-routing skeleton and the full copy-extraction to exist first, not just no-conflict). (f) SIZE: does REQ-003 (routing array edit + en.json seeding) still fit one turn now that the switcher-code work dropped out, or did REQ-ANALYST's finding change the SIZE calculus for the better without them re-checking whether REQ-003 is now almost too small to justify being separate from REQ-004 (assess, don't assume either way).
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-e from WF-01_requirement_development.md Step 2 are each explicitly run and recorded against both REQ-003 and REQ-004
REQ-ANALYST's LocaleSwitcher.tsx staleness finding is independently re-verified by opening that file directly, not taken on trust
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and check letter, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail example shape
If PASS, result.summary states what was independently re-derived (which file was opened, which specific criteria were checked against which text), not just 'looks good'
